latest_final: A prisoner arranged with a prison guard to help him escape: the guard was to dig him out after his coffin had been buried. The guard agreed to help, but died in prison before the escape plan was carried out. The prisoner did not know the guard had died. He entered the coffin after the guard’s death, believing it contained the body of the person whose funeral was taking place, though he did not know whose funeral it was or that the body was his accomplice. The coffin was buried with the funeral-goers believing it contained only the guard’s body; they did not know the prisoner was inside. In the darkness, the prisoner struck a match, recognized the guard, and realized that the one person expected to rescue him was dead. No one else was meant to dig him out, and he could not open the coffin from inside. Trapped underground, he died. The answers do not establish why he believed the funeral was for someone other than the guard, so that detail cannot be supplied with confidence.
